title: A Combined Information-Theoretic, Oscillation, and Geophysical Bound on Joint Neutrino Communication and Earth Tomography
content: Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) using trans-terrestrial neutrino beams has been proposed as a dual-purpose medium for both high-rate data transfer and Earth density tomography. We rigorously formalize the end-to-end information-theoretic, oscillation-physical, and geophysical constraints of such a facility, testing an illustrative 5% core density measurement in 0.36 years (54 \(\mu\)bit/s) as a representative optimistic benchmark. We demonstrate that such naive estimates originate from a fundamental mathematical error: conflating the peak and average event rates in the Fisher information, which underestimates the required integration time by the peak-to-average power ratio (\(\rho \sim 10^4\)). By establishing a unified Poisson channel model subject to realistic power constraints, we show that the high modulation required for high-rate communication inherently suppresses tomographic sensitivity. Furthermore, we prove that the exact Mikheyev-Smirnov-Wolfenstein (MSW) resonance is a density-sensitivity minimum, and wave-packet separation at antipodal baselines suppresses the oscillatory phase derivative. Integrating these effects with full 3-flavor PMNS evolution, 10-shell PREM integration, and a Toy Monte Carlo injection-recovery test, we establish a robust combined bound specific to antipodal core tomography. Realistic model variations yield a required integration time of \(\sim 2,400\) to \(13,500\) years, while even an unphysical zero-decoherence assumption yields a theoretical floor of 185 years. Additionally, for drift rates of \(0.1\%\)/millennium, geophysical non-stationarity becomes comparable to the statistical error at \(T_{\mathrm{cross}}\sim 10^4\) years. A comprehensive numerical defence suite—including exact Poisson profiling, geophysical drift simulation, and energy scale degeneracy—demonstrates that even a 1% energy miscalibration inflates the required time to \(>3 \times 10^5\) years. A Kullback-Leibler divergence analysis yields a statistically meaningless \(0.07\sigma\) separation for the 0.36-year benchmark. We provide exact scaling laws and establish the precise megawatt-scale resource integral (\(P_{\mathrm{avg}} M \cdot T_{5\%} \gtrsim 10^9\) MW\(\cdot\)kt\(\cdot\)yr) required for future geophysical facilities.
